transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Verdant), Janelle Reed (Verdant), Marcus Lee (Verdant)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review quality evaluation results, discuss prompt tuning and regression checks, and plan next steps (security docs, regression bench, prompts).

Topics: quality metrics, scoring thresholds, prompt set v2, guardrails, regression test plan, infra constraints (VPC/KMS), rollout strategy.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, I think we have about 45 minutes. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Samir Gupta: Good, thanks. Busy week but looking forward to the results.
[00:10] Priya Shah: Quick agenda — run through the latest quality evals, show a few failed cases, discuss prompt tweaks, then action items.
[00:18] Janelle Reed: Sounds good. We're hoping to see improvement on the product extraction prompts and fewer hallucinations on entity fields.
[00:25] Alex Martinez: Yep — great. Okay, Priya, you want to start with the scoring summary?
[00:28] Priya Shah: Sure. So we ran the v1 baseline and the new prompt set v2 against the 2k-case benchmark. High level: overall pass rate moved from 73% to 81% using the new prompts and the soft-scoring thresholds. Precision on entity extraction improved from 0.68 to 0.76, recall up slightly.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: That's encouraging. Did you see any latency regressions when running v2 with the longer prompt context?
[00:50] Priya Shah: Minimal — token overhead added around 20-40ms median per request on our dedicated setup; the Redwood dedicated nodes handled batching well. There was a small bump in 99th percentile, we think due to KV cache warmup.
[01:05] Samir Gupta: When you say KV cache — is that the Redis cache or the runtime kv cache? We saw references to both in the doc and want to make sure it's the right thing.
[01:12] Priya Shah: Sorry yeah — this is the runtime KV cache — the per-request key-value cache that stores prefixes. Not Redis. The docs might call it kv-cache or key cache, sometimes the transcription spells it wrong.
[01:22] Janelle Reed: On the scoring side, can you explain the soft-scoring thresholds? We had a couple of cases flagged as false negative by our team.
[01:28] Priya Shah: Right — soft-scoring is where we accept partial matches and weight different fields; we lower the threshold for non-critical fields like product description but keep strict thresholds for identifiers like SKU. The false negatives you saw were borderline because we tightened SKU matching.
[01:42] Marcus Lee: It would help if we had an explicit mapping of field importance so we can align on business tolerance.
[01:47] Alex Martinez: We'll include that in the scoring sheet — mapping priority: SKU (high), product_name (high), price (medium), description (low).
[01:55] Samir Gupta: One thing we noticed — the model sometimes invents vendor names for missing values. That's a hallucination type we want to trap. Any guardrails on hallucinations?
[02:03] Priya Shah: Yes — we've got a two-layer guardrail. First is prompt-level guardrails: instructions to respond with 'UNKNOWN' for missing fields. Second is post-processing: answer normalization + a hallucination detector that scores confidence; below threshold we return 'UNKNOWN' or route to human review. The detector flags low-semantic-similarity outputs.
[02:20] Janelle Reed: Is that the Redwood 'safety filter' or something in our POC code?
[02:24] Priya Shah: It's a combination — Redwood offers built-in output filters and you can add app-level heuristics. In our run we used Redwood's filter plus a custom regex-based rule for vendor formats.
[02:35] Samir Gupta: On security — we need confirmation that logs with PII get redacted before leaving our VPC. We also need KMS integration details.
[02:42] Alex Martinez: Understood — we'll share the security pack. Quick note: in Dedicated and Private modes we support customer-managed KMS and VPC-only egress. Priya, can you flag the specific doc?
[02:52] Priya Shah: I'll send the security brief. For Dedicated we can enable KMS integration and restrict logs. I'll add the exact audit log retention and fields that are redacted.
[03:03] Marcus Lee: On the regression tests — you mentioned a targeted bench?
[03:07] Priya Shah: Yes. Plan: run the regression bench of 500 targeted edge cases that previously failed + 1k random cases. We'll compare v1 -> v2 and produce a delta report with per-field diffs and examples. Expect an initial pass tomorrow and a full report by next Tuesday.
[03:20] Samir Gupta: Good. How do we handle the cases where v2 improves one field but degrades another? Historically it's been tricky.
[03:26] Alex Martinez: We use the scoring weights; if a high-priority field drops, we either roll back that prompt change or do an A/B canary with fallback to v1 for high-priority routes. Redwood supports per-route rollouts and automatic fallback.
[03:39] Janelle Reed: That sounds promising. What's the overhead to maintain two prompt sets in production?
[03:44] Priya Shah: Minimal from infra side — it's mostly orchestration. There's config to pin model versions and prompt sets per route. Cost-wise you pay for the extra eval traffic but the runtime supports split traffic for canary.
[03:55] Marcus Lee: Any notes on quantization or model variant we used? I saw v2 ran against 'redwood-optim-3b-quant' in the sheet.
[04:02] Priya Shah: Yes, we used a quantized 3B variant for cost reasons. There was a slight hit in recall on some long context examples vs the full float model, but throughput and cost improved significantly. We can re-run critical cases on the float model if needed.
[04:18] Samir Gupta: Competitor question — we heard Cobalt AI has a built-in entity extraction suite. How do we compare on maintenance overhead?
[04:25] Alex Martinez: Cobalt has good out-of-the-box extraction but less flexible routing and cost controls. Redwood's differential is observability and the ability to pin variants across Dedicated/Private. We'll share a short comparison doc.
[04:36] Priya Shah: Quick demo — I have three examples of failed cases from the 2k run, I'll read them out.
[04:41] [screen share noises, brief pause] 
[04:44] Priya Shah: Case A: Input missing price, model returned a fabricated price 'approx $49.99' — we marked as hallucination. With prompt v2 we add explicit "If price unknown write UNKNOWN" and post-process to map fabricated prices to UNKNOWN if heuristics fail. Now shows UNKNOWN.
[04:59] Janelle Reed: Nice. Case B?
[05:01] Priya Shah: Case B: product_description got truncated and merged with next item when the prompt included long catalog context. We introduced a context window trim and rephrased the instruction to prioritize current record. Fix reduced truncation errors by 60%.
[05:17] Marcus Lee: Those fixes look solid. Any differences in the leaderboard of failing types?
[05:22] Priya Shah: Top fails: hallucinated vendor (25%), SKU mismatch (20%), truncated description (15%), price normalization (12%). Others are low-frequency.
[05:31] Samir Gupta: For the hallucination cases, can we get the specific heuristics (regex or scoring) you used?
[05:36] Priya Shah: I'll include them in the scoring sheet. For vendor we use an NER + vendor whitelist and a confidence threshold — below threshold mark UNKNOWN.
[05:44] Janelle Reed: Regarding deployment timeline — we're targeting a pilot rollout to 2 internal teams by end of month. Does that timeline still make sense?
[05:51] Alex Martinez: Yes assuming regression benchmark shows no critical regressions. We have the rollout plan: canary 10% with automatic fallback, then 50% if metrics stable, then full. We'll also attach alerting for quality drops.
[06:04] Samir Gupta: Alerting — what thresholds would you recommend?
[06:07] Priya Shah: Recommended: drop in overall pass rate >3% or spike in hallucination rate >2% triggers an alert. We can customize.
[06:15] Marcus Lee: Who owns the alerts on our side? We want push to PagerDuty for infra and email for Product.
[06:20] Alex Martinez: We'll wire it to both. Redwood console supports webhook destinations and PagerDuty integration.
[06:28] Janelle Reed: A couple of housekeeping items — please put the updated prompts in the repo, not just a GDrive doc; it's easier for our CI to pull.
[06:35] Priya Shah: Will do, I'll push them to the repo and include examples.
[06:38] Samir Gupta: Anything else on tests or security?
[06:41] Marcus Lee: One more ask — can Redwood provide redaction examples from the log pipeline so we can validate nothing sensitive leaks during the POC?
[06:48] Alex Martinez: Yes, we'll include sanitized samples in the security packet.
[06:52] Priya Shah: Recap of next steps: 1) Alex to share prompt set v2 + scoring sheet; 2) Priya to run targeted regression bench and share delta report; 3) Samir to share PII redaction rules + schema; 4) schedule security review (Alex to propose times).
[07:07] Janelle Reed: That's perfect. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
[07:11] Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the docs and the calendar invite for the security review.
[07:18] Samir Gupta: Thanks all, talk soon.

End recap (auto):

- Guardrails: prompt-level 'UNKNOWN' rule + post-process hallucination detector in place.
- Regression bench planned (500 targeted + 1k random) with results by next Tue.
- Security docs and redaction examples to be shared; KMS/VPC options confirmed available for Dedicated/Private.
